Chennai City Municipal Corporation Act, 1919
Act
No. 4 of 1919
Statement of Objects and Reasons - Madras City Municipal Corporation and District Municipalities (Amendment) Act,
1962 (Tamil Nadu Act 10 of 1962) - Under the Madras City Municipal Corporation Act, 1919 (Madras Act IV of 1919) and
the Madras District Municipalities Act, 1920 (Madras Act V of 1920), the ordinary elections shall take place on such days
in the months of August and September immediately preceding ordinary vacancies. It is proposed to make provisions in
the said Acts to fix dates of ordinary election within three months before the occurrence of ordinary vacancies and not
necessarily in the months of August and September as at present.

2. It is also proposed to incorporate in the said Acts provisions in respect of the following matters relating to the holding
of elections on the lines of the provisions made in the Madras Panchayats Act, 1958, namely :-
Page 1/275
 
Chennai City Municipal Corporation Act, 1919
(a) power to extend or reduce the term of office of councillors as a who for a period not exceeding three months ;
(b) power to direct, holding of any ordinary election even after the occurrence of the vacancies; and
(c) power to postpone or alter the dates of ordinary or casual elections.

3. Under the provisions of the said Acts, it is obligatory to fill up casual vacancies except vacancies occurring within
three months before the ordinary date of retirement of councillors. It is considered that it is not necessary to conduct
casual elections to fill casual vacancies arising within a period of six months prior to the ordinary date of retirement of
councillors. It is accordingly proposed to make provisions in the said Acts for dispensing with the holding of such casual
elections on the eve of ordinary elections.

4. For the purposes of elections to Municipal Councils and the Corporation of Madras, the electoral rolls are prepared on
the basis of the electoral roll for territorial constituency of the Madras Legislative Assembly relating to the municipality or
the Corporation. As the names of service electors (Armed Forces personnel and absentee officers) are included in a
separate part of the electoral roll for the Assembly without specifying their addresses, it is found difficult to include their
names in the electoral rolls prepared under the said Acts for purposes of election to Municipal Councils and the
Corporation of Madras. It is, therefore, proposed to publish the electoral rolls relating to municipalities and the
Corporation of Madras without including the names of service electors unless such electors apply for inclusion of their
names in the electoral roll to the authorities concerned by giving particulars of their addresses in the local area
concerned.

5. It is also considered desirable to incorporate in the said Acts provisions similar to those contained in the
Representation of People Act, 1951 (Central Act XLIII of 1951) and the Madras District Boards Act, 1920 (Madras Act
XIV of 1920) relating to electoral offences and requisitioning of premises, vehicles, vessels and animals. For the purpose
of effectively combating the evil of personation of voters at municipal elections, it is considered necessary to make
provision in the said Acts for enhanced punishment with a minimum penalty of imprisonment for a term of not less than
six months and fine for the offence of personation punishable under section 17-F of the Indian Penal Code.

6. The Bill seeks to give effect to the above objects. Certain consequential and minor amendments to the said Act have
also been incorporated.
Published in Part IV - Section 3 of the Tamil Nadu Government Gazette Extraordinary, dated the 18th July 1972.
Statement of Objects and Reasons - Madras City Municipal Corporation (Amendment) Act, 1972 (Tamil Nadu Act 25 of
2972). - There are at present four classes of officers and servants under the establishment of the Municipal Corporation
of Madras. The council of the Municipal Corporation of Madras has suggested that appointments to posts included in
Classes III and IV should be made by the commissioner instead of selection being made by the appointments committee
and the appointment being made by the commissioner as at present. The Government have accepted the suggestion of
the council and have decided to amend section 85 of the Madras City Municipal Corporation Act, 1919 (Tamil Nadu Act
IV of 1919), suitably for the purpose.

2. The Bill seeks to give effect to the above decision.
Published in Part IV-Section 3 of the Tamil Nadu Government Gazette Extraordinary, dated the 12th August 1972.
Statement of Objects and Reasons - Madras City Municipal Corporation and Madurai City Municipal Corporation
(Amendment) Act, 1972 (Tamil Nadu Act 7 of 1973. - Under section 5 of the Madras City Municipal Corporation Act,
1919 (Tamil Nadu Act IV of 1919), the council of the municipal corporation of Madras shall consist of one hundred and
twenty councillors. Section 45 of the said Act provides that the city shall be divided into one hundred and twenty
territorial divisions. Sub-section (1) of section 6 lays down that each of the territorial constituencies of the Tamil Nadu
Legislative Assembly in the city' shall be a circle for the purpose of the municipal government of the City of Madras.
Consequent on the abolition of the circle and central committees in i971, the council of the municipal corporation of
Madras has suggested (i) to do away with circles and the principle of equating the circles with the Assembly
Constituencies; and (ii) to increase the number of territorial divisions from 120 to 150. The Government have accepted
the above suggestions and decided to amend the Act. Consequently, it has also been decided to increase the minimum
number of Scheduled Castes or Scheduled Tribes and women to be 15 and 8 respectively and also to increase the
quorum for the council from thirty-three to fifty.

2. Sub-section (2)(d) of section 6-D of the Madras City Municipal Corporation Act, 1919 (Tamil Nadu Act IV of 1919) and
sub-section (3)(d) of section 9 of the Madurai City Municipal Corporation Act, 1971 (Tamil Nadu Act
15 of 1971
) empower the standing committee on accounts to write off only the amount of any loss of, or any depreciation caused
Page 2/275
 
Chennai City Municipal Corporation Act, 1919
to, the municipal property which in the opinion of the committee is irrecoverable. There is no monetary limit to write off in
the case of Madras Corporation whereas in the case of Madurai Corporation the power is restricted only up to Rs. 1,000.
As the said provisions do not empower the said committee to write off any tax, fee or other amount, whatsoever due to
the corporation whether under a contract or otherwise or any sum payable in connection therewith, if it appears to the
committee to be irrecoverable, it has been decided to amend the Tamil Nadu Act IV of 1919 and the Tamil Nadu Act
15 of 1971
accordingly.

3. The Bill seeks to give effect to the above decisions.
Published in Part IV-Section 3 of the Tamil Nadu Government Gazette Extraordinary, dated the 6th December 1972.
Statement of Objects and Reasons - Madras City Municipal Corporation (Amendment) Act, 1980 (Tamil Nadu Act 19 of
1980)2. - Under sub-section (1) of section 55-B of the Madras City Municipal Corporation Act, 1919 (Tamil Nadu Act IV
of 1919), the period within which the Special Officer of the Municipal Corporation of Madras should make arrangements
for the conduct of elections to the council of the Corporation of Madras been fixed as five years and six months from the
30th November 1974 with a provision that the State Government may, by notification, for sufficient cause direct that the
period specified shall be reduced by such period, not exceeding six months as may be specified in such notification. It
has been decided to prepare the Madras Corporation Electoral Rolls by adapting the relevant Assembly Electoral Rolls
as basic roll. The said Assembly Electoral Rolls have been revised summarily for inclusion of persons who have attained
21years of age on the 1st January 1980 and published on the 22nd March 1980. The Tamil Nadu Legislative Assembly
elections have recently been held. The Madras Corporation Electoral Rolls will have to be prepared and the elections to
the council of Corporation of Madras will have to be held. The elections to the council of the Corporation of Madras could
not be held before the 31st May 1980.

2. The Government have, therefore, decided to extend the period within which the Special Officer should make
arrangements for the conduct of elections to the council of the Corporation of Madras, for a further period of one year
from the 31st May 1980. Accordingly, the Madras City Municipal Corporation Amendment) Ordinance, 1980 (Tamil Nadu
Ordinance 6 of 1980) was promulgated by the Governor to achieve the above object.

3. This Bill seeks to replace the said Ordinance.
Published in Part IV-Section 1 of the Tamil Nadu Government Gazette Extraordinary, dated the 26th June 1980.
Statement of Objects and Reasons - Tamil Nadu Local Authorities' laws (Amendment) Act, 1980 (Tamil Nadu Act 32 of
1980). - Section 47 of the Madras City Municipal Corporation Act, 1919 (Tamil Nadu Act IV of 1919), section 51 of the
Madurai City Municipal Corporation Act, 1971 (Tamil Nadu Act
15 of 1971
), section 44 of the Tamil Nadu District Municipalities Act, 1920 (Tamil Nadu Act V of 1920) and section 20 of the Tamil
Nadu Panchayats Act, 1958 (Tamil Nadu Act XXXV of 1958) provide that every person who is qualified to be included in
such part of the electoral rolls of the Legislative Assembly Constituency as relates to the municipal corporations,
municipalities and Panchayats shall be entitled to be included in the electoral roll of the respective local body. The
electoral rolls of the Legislative Assembly Constituencies are those prepared under the Representation of the People
Act, 1950 (Central Act XLIII of 1950) and under that Act, persons who are not less than twenty-one years of age are
entitled to be registered in the electoral roll.

2. Recently, in States like Kerala, Andhra Pradesh, Rajasthan and West Bengal, the voting age for the elections to the
local authorities have been reduced to eighteen years. An all party leaders meeting was held in the Secretariat on the
11th July 1980 to discuss about reducing the voting age from twenty-one to eighteen years for the elections to the local
bodies. Most of the party leaders were in favour of reducing the voting age as eighteen years from twenty-one. The
Government accordingly decided to reduce the voting age for the elections to the local bodies in this State as eighteen
years. 11 has also been decided to fix the minimum age for the contesting candidates in elections to the local bodies as
twenty-one years. It has further been decided that only those persons who are able to read and write in Tamil shall be
qualified to stand for election as chairmen of Panchayat union councils.

3. The Bill seeks to achieve the above decisions.
Published in Part IV-Section 1 of the Tamil Nadu Government Gazette Extraordinary, dated the 5th August 1980.
Statement of Objects and Reasons - Madras City Municipal Corporation (Amendment) Act, 1981 (Tamil Nadu Act 17 of
1981). - Under sub-section (1) of section 55-B of the Madras City Municipal Corporation Act, 1919 (Tamil Nadu Act IV of
1919), as subsequently amended, the period within which the Special Officer of the Municipal Corporation of Madras
Page 3/275
 
Chennai City Municipal Corporation Act, 1919
should make arrangements for the conduct of elections to the council of the Corporation of Madras has been fixed as six
years and six months from the 30th November 1974. The period expires on the 30th May 1981.

2. The Commissioner, Corporation of Madras, has been entrusted with the census work. The Government of India have
requested the State Government not to entrust any other important work to the Commissioner, Corporation of Madras,
until the census work is over. The electoral rolls of the Corporation of Madras can be prepared only after the census
work is over. The elections to council of the Corporation of Madras could not, therefore, be held before the 30th May

1981.
3. The Government have, therefore, decided to extend the period within which arrangements should be made for the
conduct of elections to the Municipal Corporation of Madras by the Special Officer of the Municipal Corporation of
Madras for a further period of one year beyond the 30th May 1981 and to amend the Madras City Municipal Corporation
Act, 1919 for the purpose, with the existing provision to reduce the extended period by a period not exceeding six
months in case it is found possible to conduct the elections earlier.

4. The Bill seeks to give effect to the above decision.
Published in Part IV-Section 1 of the Tamil Nadu Government Gazette Extraordinary, dated the 2nd March 1981.
Statement of Objects and Reasons - Madras City Municipal Corporation (Amendment) Act, 1983 (Tamil Nadu Act 13 of
1983). - Under sub-section (1) of section 55-B of the Madras City Municipal Corporation Act, 1919 (Tamil Nadu Act IV of
1919), as subsequently amended, the period within which the Special Officer of the Municipal Corporation of Madras
should make arrangements for the conduct of elections to the council of the Corporation of Madras has been fixed as
eight years and six months from the 30th November 1974. The said period will expire on the 30th May 1983.

2. A policy decision was taken by the Government that ordinary elections to Panchayats may be conducted first and
then to conduct elections to the municipalities and municipal corporations, so that the feasibility of introducing the
reservation of seats for the members of Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes and for women in municipalities and
municipal corporations may be examined. A civil appeal challenging the decision of the Madras High Court upholding
the reservations of the office of presidents of Panchayats and chairmen of Panchayat union councils for the members of
Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes and for women, is now pending before the Supreme Court. The Government
have filed an expedition petition in the Supreme Court, to fix an early date for the disposal of the case. Apart from this,
before conducting elections to the Municipal Corporation of Madras, the electoral rolls have to be prepared afresh by
house-to-house enumeration with the 1st January 1983 as the qualifying date. It will take a minimum period of six
months. Hence, it is not possible to conduct the elections to the municipal corporation of Madras before the 30th May

1983. It has, therefore, become necessary to extend the period within which arrangements should be made for the
conduct of elections to the municipal corporation of Madras by the Special Officer of the municipal corporation of Madras
beyond the 30th May 1983.

3. The Government have, accordingly decided to further extend the said period for one year beyond the 30th May 1983
and to amend the said Madras City Municipal Corporation Act, 1919 (Tamil Nadu Act IV of 1919) for the purpose,
retaining the existing provision to reduce the extended period by a period not exceeding six months, in case it becomes
possible to conduct the elections earlier.

4. The Bill seeks to give effect to the above decision.
Published in Part IV-Section 1 of the Tamil Nadu Government Gazette Extraordinary, dated the 4th March 1983.
Statement of Objects and Reasons - Tamil Nadu Municipal Laws (Amendment) Act, 1985 (Tamil Nadu Act 32 of 1985). -
Section 97 of the Madras City Municipal Corporation Act, 1919 (Tamil Nadu Act IV of 1919) empowers the State
Government to transfer any officer or servant of the corporation to the service of any municipality or to transfer any
officer or servant of any such municipality to the service of the corporation. There is no provision in the said Act
empowering the State Government to transfer any officer or servant of the corporation to the service of other municipal
corporations in the State such as municipal corporation of Madurai and Coimbatore.

2. Section 114 of the Madurai City Municipal Corporation Act, 1971 (Tamil Nadu Act
15 of 1971
) empowers the State Government to transfer any officer or servant of the corporation to the service of the municipal
corporation of Madras or of an)' municipality and vice versa. There is no provision in the said Tamil Nadu Act
15 of 1971
empowering the State Government to transfer any officer or servant of the corporation to the service of the municipal
corporation of Coimbatore.
Page 4/275
 
Chennai City Municipal Corporation Act, 1919

3. Section 116 of the Coimbatore City Municipal Corporation Act, 1981 (Tamil Nadu Act
25 of 1981
) empowers the State Government to transfer any officer or servant of the corporation to the service of the municipal
corporation of Madras or to the municipal corporation of Madurai or to any other municipal corporation that may be
constituted under any law for the time being in force, or to any municipality and vice versa.

4. Section 73-A of the Tamil Nadu District Municipalities Act, 1920 (Tamil Nadu Act V of 1920) empowers the State
Government to transfer any officer or servant of a municipality to the service of another municipality, after consulting the
municipalities concerned.

5. The Government consider that with a view to toning up the administration of the municipal corporations and
municipalities in the State and to render better service to the public, the employees of any one municipal corporation
shall be made liable to be transferred to any other municipal corporation or municipality and the employees of the
municipalities to any of the municipal corporations which is now in existence and which may be newly constituted and to
any other municipality. It has, therefore, been decided to amend the said Tamil Nadu Act IV of 1919, Tamil Nadu Act V
of 1920, Tamil Nadu Act
15 of 1971
and Tamil Nadu Act
25 of 1981
to achieve the object in view.

6. The Bill seeks to give effect to the above decision.
Published in Part IV-Section 1 of the Tamil Nadu Government Gazette Extraordinary in the year 1985.
Statement of Objects and Reasons - Madras City Municipal Corporation (Amendment) Act, 1985 (Tamil Nadu Act 5 of
1985). - Under sub-section (1) of section 55-B of the Madras City Municipal Corporation Act, 1919 (Tamil Nadu Act IV of
1919), as subsequently amended, the period within which the Special Officer of the Municipal Corporation of Madras
should make arrangements for the conduct of elections to the council of the Corporation of Madras had been fixed as
nine years and six months from the 30th November, 1974. The said period was due to expire on the 30th May 1984.

2. The Government have decided to issue identity cards with or without photographs affixed thereon to all the voters in
the City of Madras, City of Madurai and City of Coimbatore as well as in all the municipalities and then to conduct civic
elections to the Corporation councils and to the municipal councils. Accordingly, arrangements are being made to
provide the aforesaid identity cards to the voters. It become therefore, necessary to further extend the period within
which the arrangements should be made for the conduct of elections to the Municipal Corporation of Madras by the
Special Officer beyond the 30th May 1984.

3. The Government accordingly decided to amend the said Madras City Municipal Corporation Act, 1919 (Tamil Nadu
Act IV of 1919), so as to extend the said period by a further period of one year beyond the 30th May 1984. To give effect
to the above decision, the Madras City Municipal Corporation (Amendment) Ordinance, 1984 (Tamil Nadu Ordinance 6
of 1984) was promulgated by the Governor and published in the Tamil Nadu Government Gazette, Extraordinary, dated
the 30th May, 1984.

4. A Bill to replace the said Ordinance was introduced in the Tamil Nadu Legislative Assembly on the 9th October 1984,
in its session which commenced on the 8th October 1984. The said Bill was passed in the Legislative Assembly on the
12th October, 1984. But, the said Bill could not be taken up for consideration by the Tamil Nadu Legislative Council,
because the Legislative Council was adjourned sine die on the 15th October 1984. Subsequently the Legislative
Assembly was dissolved. As such the Bill, as passed by the Legislative Assembly, could not become an Act of the
Legislature to replace the said Ordinance in time. In view of the circumstances stated above, it become necessary to
promulgate again an Ordinance for the purpose. Accordingly, the Madras City (Tamil Nadu Ordinance 19 of 1984) was
promulgated by the Governor on the 19th November 1984 and the same was published in the Tamil Nadu Government
Gazette, Extraordinary, dated the 20th November 1984. Since the elections to the Council of the Corporation of Madras
cannot be conducted before the 30th May 1985, that is the period within which the arrangements should be made for the
conduct of the elections as extended by the Tamil Nadu Ordinance 19 of 1984, it has also been decided to extend the
said period upto the 30th November 1985.

5. The Bill seeks to replace the said Ordinance by an act of the Legislature and also to give effect to the above decision.
Published in Part IV-Section 1 of the Tamil Nadu Government Gazette Extraordinary, dated the 14th March 1985.
Statement of Objects and Reasons - Tamil Nadu Municipal Corporation Laws (Amendment) Act, 1987 (Tamil Nadu Act
Page 5/275
 
Chennai City Municipal Corporation Act, 1919
14 of 1987. - It has been decided by the Government to undertake a common legislation applicable to all the Municipal
Corporations in the State and a draft Bill for the purpose is under preparation. In that connection, the administrative set
up obtaining in the Municipal Corporations of Bombay, Calcutta and Howrah are also being taken into account with a
view to decide a suitable administrative set up for the Municipal Corporations in this State. The Bill which is under
preparation is likely to be introduced in the next session of the Legislative Assembly and the same will become an Act
after obtaining the assent of the President thereto. After the enactment of the proposed Act, necessary rules will also
have to be framed for its implementation and it will take quite some time.

2. The Government have decided to hold elections to the Municipal Co-operations of the cities of Madras, Madurai and
Coimbatore under the proposed common legislation. In the meanwhile, the terms for which Special Officers were
appointed to the Municipal Corporations of the cities of Madras, Madurai and Coimbatore are due to expire between the
30th May 1987 and the 29th July 1987. In view of the above, it has become necessary to extend by one year the period
for which the Special Officers were appointed. It has, therefore, been decided to amend the Madras City Municipal
Corporation Act, 1919 (Tamil Nadu Act IV of 1919), the Madurai City Municipal Corporation Act, 1971 (Tamil Nadu Act
15 of 1971
) and the Coimbatore City Municipal Corporation Act, 1981 (Tamil Nadu Act
25 of 1981
) suitably for the purpose.

3. The Bill seeks to achieve the above object.
Published in Part IV-Section 1 of the Tamil Nadu Govt. Gazette Extraordinary, dated the 28th April, 1987.
Statement of Objects and Reasons - Tamil Nadu Municipal Corporation Laws (Third Amendment) Act, 1989 (Tamil Nadu
Act IS of 1989). - Under the laws relating to the Municipal Corporations in Tamil Nadu, provision has been made for
representation of Scheduled Castes, or Scheduled Tribes and women from among the elected members of the Council
on the following scale :-
d Castes or Scheduled Tribes
Women
The Madras City Municipal Corporation

2. It is also provided that where the aforesaid number of members are not elected from among the Scheduled Castes,
Scheduled Tribes or women, the Council is empowered to co-opt such numbers of persons to make up the deficiency.

3. It is now proposed to give more representation to persons belonging to Scheduled Castes or Scheduled Tribes and
women in the respective Councils of the Municipal Corporations on the following scale :-
d Castes & Scheduled Tribes
Women

4. The Bill seeks to achieve the above object.

Published in Part IV-Section 1 of the Tamil Nadu Government Gazette Extraordinary, dated the 3rd May,
Statement of Objects and Reasons - Tamil Nadu Municipal Corporation (Special Provisions and Amendment) Act, 1989
(Tamil Nadu Act 5 of 1989). - The Government have decided to conduct the elections to the Municipal Corporations of
Madras, Madurai and Coimbatore in April, 1989. The Municipal Corporation Laws provide eighteen years as the
minimum age for voting. The electoral rolls for the said Municipal Corporations have not yet been prepared in
accordance with the said Laws. It would take quite a long time for the preparation of electoral rolls afresh with eighteen
years as the minimum age for voting. Since the Government have decided to conduct elections to the said Municipal
Corporations during April 1989, there is no other alternative except to hold the elections on the basis of the existing
electoral rolls for the territorial constituencies of the Tamil. Nadu Legislative Assembly, with twenty-one years as the
qualifying age, as relate to the divisions or wards of the said Municipal Corporations. For this purpose, the Government
have decided to make special provisions applicable only for the ensuing elections to the said Municipal Corporations.

2. The Government have also decided to reduce the term of office of the councillors of the said Municipal Corporations
from six years to five years and the term of office of Mayors and Deputy Mayors of the said Municipal Corporations from
two years to one year and to amend the Madras City Municipal Corporation Act, 1919 (Tamil Nadu Act IV of 1919), the
Madurai City Municipal Corporation Act, 1971 (Tamil Nadu Act
15 of 1971
) and the Coimbatore City Municipal Corporation Act, 1981 (Tamil Nadu Act
25 of 1981
) for the purpose suitably.

3. The Bill seeks to give effect to the above decisions.
Published in Part IV-Section 1 of the Tamil Nadu Government Gazette Extraordinary, dated 13th February 19S9.
Statement of Objects and Reasons - Tamil Nadu Municipal Corporation Laws (Second Amendment) Act, 1989 (Tamil
Nadu Act 14 of 1989). - The Government have earlier decided to hold the elections to the City Municipal Corporation of
Madras, Madurai and Coimbatore during April-May 1989 making use of the electoral rolls for the territorial constituencies
of the Tamil Nadu Legislative Assembly consisting of persons who have completed twenty-one years of age as on the
1st January 1989 and relatable to the respective divisions or wards, as the case may be, in the said Municipal
Corporations. Accordingly, special provisions in that regard were made in section 2 of the Tamil Nadu Municipal
Corporation Laws (Special Provisions and Amendment) Act, 1989 (Tamil Nadu Act 5 of 1989)

2. In view of the preparation of the electoral rolls for the Assembly Constituencies consisting of persons who have
completed eighteen years of age as on the 1st April 1989, which are under revision and expected to be finalised by June
1989, the Government have now decided to hold the elections making use of the said revised electoral rolls.

3. However, in the meanwhile, the term of office of the Special Officers of these Municipal Corporations stand to expire
between the 30th May 1989 and the 29th July 1989. As it will not be possible to hold the elections to these Municipal
Corporations before the said period, it is considered necessary to extend the term of office of the Special Officers up to
the 30th September 1989.

4. As the elections to these Municipal Corporations are not to be held during April-May 1989, it is also proposed to omit
the special provisions in that regard made in section 2 of the Tamil Nadu Municipal Corporation Laws (Special
Provisions and Amendment) Act, 1989.

5. The Bill seeks to achieve the above objects.
Published in Part IV-Section 1 of the Tamil Nadu Government Gazette Extraordinary, dated the 27th April 1989.
Statement of Objects and Reasons - Tamil Nadu Municipal Corporation Laws (Fourth Amendment) Act, 1989 (Tamil
Nadu Act 34 of 1989). - The Government have constituted a Committee to specify the divisions or wards in the Municipal
Corporations of Madras, Madurai and Coimbatore in respect of which members of the Scheduled Castes and Scheduled
Tribes and Women are to be elected to the respective councils. The recommendations of the Committee are under
consideration,

2. The term of Office of the Special Officers of the Municipal Corporations of Madras, Madurai and Coimbatore was due
to expire on the 30th September 1989. As it was considered that the publication of the final notification on reservation of
divisions and wards and the conduct of elections to the said Municipal Corporations could not be done before the 30th
September 1989, the Government decided to extend the term of office of the said Special Officers for a further period of
six months, that is, up to the 31st March 1990. Accordingly the Tamil Nadu Municipal Corporation Laws (Fourth
Amendment) Ordinance, 1989 (Tamil Nadu Ordinance 8 of 1989) was promulgated by the Governor.
Page 7/275
 
Chennai City Municipal Corporation Act, 1919

3. The Bill seeks to replace the said Ordinance.
Published in Part IV-Section I of the Tamil Nadu Government Gazette Extraordinary, dated 31.10.1989.
Statement of Objects and Reasons - Tamil Nadu Municipal Laws (Amendment) Act, 1990 (Tamil Nadu Act 19 of 1990). -
The Tamil Nadu District Municipalities Act, 1920 and the laws relating to the Municipal Corporations of Madras, Madurai
and Coimbatore prohibit the naming of public street, park, playground, bus stand, arch or municipal property after a
living person irrespective of his status or office occupied by him. The Government have now decided to omit the
prohibition above mentioned.

2. The Bill seeks to give effect to the above decision.
Published in Part IV-Section 1 of the Tamil Nadu Government Gazette Extraordinary, dated the 26th April, 1990.
Statement of Objects and Reasons - Tamil Nadu Municipal Corporation Laws (Second Amendment) Act, 1990 (Tamil
Nadu Act 27 of 1990). - The Government have decided that the strength of the Council of the Municipal Corporations of
Madras, Madurai and Coimbatore and the number of divisions or wards in the above three Corporations shall be as
follows :-
Number of divisions/ wards
Number of women to be co-opted
Total number of councillors
The Madras City Municipal Corporation

80.
2. The Government have also decided that reservation for the Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes shall be made in
the three Corporations proportionate to the percentage of their population in the respective cities.

3. The Government have also decided that thirty per cent of the total number of seats shall be reserved for women in
each of the three Corporations. In respect of Madras Corporation, the number of seats to be reserved for women will
also include the number of seats to be reserved for women belonging to the Scheduled Castes and the Scheduled
Tribes. In respect of Madurai and Coimbatore Corporations, the number of seats to be reserved for women will include
the number of seats to be reserved for w omen belonging to the Scheduled Castes and the Scheduled Tribes and also
eight number of women councillors to be co-opted to each Council of the said Corporations.

4. It has also been decided that the divisions or wards in respect of which the numbers of the Scheduled Castes and the
Scheduled Tribes and women are to be elected will be notified by the Government, from time to time.

6. The Bill seeks to give effect to the above decision.
Published in Part IV-Section 1 of the Tamil Nadu Government Gazette Extraordinary, dated the 10th May, 1990.
Statement of Objects and Reasons - Tamil Nadu Tax on Profession, Trades, Callings and Employment Act, 1992 (Tamil
Nadu Act 24 of 1992). - With a view to improve the resources of Municipal Corporations, Municipalities, Municipal
Townships, Panchayats and Panchayats, Townships, it has been decided to bring fresh legislation to provide, for the
levy of tax on professions trades, callings and employments on a revised basis adopting the new ceiling on the tax of
Rs. 2,500 per annum as provided for in the Constitution. The tax will be levied at different rates, the maximum and
Page 8/275
 
Chennai City Municipal Corporation Act, 1919
minimum for each category being specified in the Act itself leaving it to the local authority to determine the rates. As a
measure of relief for the salaried classes, it has been decided to exempt all salaried persons including Government
employees, whose salary is less than rupees one thousand and five hundred per mensem, from the proposed levy of
profession tax. The tax will be collected and retained by the respective local bodies.

2. The Bill seeks to achieve the above object.
Published in Part IV-Section 1 of the Tamil Nadu Government Gazette Extraordinary, dated the 2nd April 1992.
Statement of Objects and Reasons - Tamil Nadu Municipal Laws (Amendment) Act, 1992 (Tamil Nadu Act 14 of 1992). -
Under sub-section (2) of section 3 of the Tamil Nadu Municipal Councils (Appointment of Special Officers) Act, 1991
(Tamil Nadu Act 14 of 1991), Special Officers have been appointed to 98 Municipal Councils except Ambattur Municipal

(4) The resulting amount will be the property tax for a half year.

Statement of Objects and Reasons - Tamil Nadu Municipal Laws (Second Amendment) Act, 1998 (Tamil Nadu Act 51 of

(1) The existing Special Act (1992) may be repealed and suitable provisions for collection of profession tax may be

cent and a maximum of 35 per cent.

to the urban local body along with paying the first half-year tax, if it is found later that the particulars furnished by them

attention of the council and administration from the real issues concerning, the welfare of the people such as basic civic

atmosphere of the councils of the concerned urban local bodies is disturbed and also the conduct of the meetings of the

passing of no-confidence motions are considered to be democratic rights, frequent use and misuse of the same will
affect the very same democracy.

54C.
Corrupt practices.
- The following shall be deemed to be corrupt practices for the purposes of this Act:-
(1)
Bribery as defined in clause (1) of section 123 of the Representation of the People Act, 1951 (Central Act XLIII of 1951).
(2)
Undue influence as defined in clause (2) of the said section.
(3)
The systematic appeal by a candidate or his agent or by any other person to vote or refrain from voting on grounds of
caste, race, community or religion or the use of or appeal to, religious symbols, or the use of or appeal to, national
symbols such as the national flag or the national emblem, for the furtherance of the prospects of that candidate's
election.
(4)
The publication by a candidate or his agent or by any other person of any statement of fact which is false, and which he
either believes to be false or does not believe to be true, in relation to the personal character or conduct of any
candidate, or in relation to the candidature, or withdrawal from contest of any candidate being a statement reasonably
calculated to prejudice the prospects of that candidate's election.
(5)
The hiring or procuring whether on payment or otherwise of any vehicle or vessel by a candidate or his agent or by any
other person for the conveyance of any elector (other than the candidate himself, and the members of his family or his
agent) to or from any polling station provided in accordance with the rules made under this Act:
Provided that the hiring of a vehicle or vessel by an elector or by several electors at their joint costs for the purpose of
conveying him or them to or from any such polling station shall not be deemed to be a corrupt practice under this clause
if the- vehicle or vessel so hired is a vehicle or vessel not propelled by mechanical power:

clause. Explanation. - In this clause the expression "vehicle" means any vehicle used or capable of being used for the
purpose of road transport whether propelled by mechanical power or otherwise and whether used for drawing other
vehicles or otherwise.

particulars of an election meeting or routine instructions to election agents or workers.

311.
Duty of commissioner to inspect.
- It shall be the duty of the commissioner to make provision for the constant and vigilant inspection of animals,
carcasses, meat, poultry, game, flesh, fish, fruit, vegetables, com, bread, flour, milk, ghee, butter, oil and any other
articles exposed or hawked about for sale or deposited in or brought to any place for the purpose of sale or of
preparation for sale.

312.
Powers of commissioner for purposes of inspection.
(1)
The commissioner or any person authorised by him in writing for the purpose, may, without notice, enter any
slaughter-house or any place where animals, poultry or fish intended for food are exposed for sale or where articles of
food are being manufactured or exposed for sale, at any time by day or night, when the slaughter, exposure for sale or
manufacture is being carried on and inspect the same and any utensil or vessel used for manufacturing, preparing or
containing any such article.
(2)
If the commissioner or any person so authorized by him has reason to believe that in any place any animal intended for
human food is being slaughtered or any carcass is being skinned or cut up or that any food is being manufactured,
stored, prepared, packed, cleansed, kept or exposed for sale, or sold without, or otherwise than in conformity with a
licence, he may enter any such place without notice at any time by day or night for the purpose of satisfying himself
whether any provision of law, by-laws, or regulations or any condition of licence is being contravened.
(3)
No claim shall lie against the commissioner or any person acting under his authority or the corporation for any damage
or inconvenience caused by the exercise of powers under this section or by the use of any force necessary for effecting
any entry into any place under this section.
(4)
In any legal proceedings in respect of powers exercised under this section in which it is alleged that any animals,
poultry, fish or articles of food were not kept, exposed, hawked about, manufactured, prepared, stored, ; packed, or
cleansed for sale, or were not intended for human food, the burden of proof shall lie on the party so alleging.
